paper_metadata.title: Empirical Evaluation of Quantum Kernel Learning for Sector Rotation Prediction: Using Fama–French 10 Industry Portfolios

summary: The paper evaluates a ZZFeatureMap-based fidelity quantum kernel on the Fama–French 10 Industry Portfolios (1,506 trading days, 2022–2024) using a 9-feature binary sector-rotation classification task. The quantum kernel achieved 55.0% accuracy on NoDur and 52.2% on Manuf, but the classical RBF baseline had the best overall mean accuracy at 52.1% versus 50.0% for the quantum method; the quantum kernel also had the lowest sector-wise standard deviation at 3.2%.

experiments.description: Quantum kernel learning for sector rotation prediction on Fama–French 10 Industry Portfolios using a ZZFeatureMap fidelity kernel and 1-nearest-neighbor classification, compared against classical SVC baselines.

algorithm.variant: fidelity quantum kernel learning with ZZFeatureMap and 1-NN classifier

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Nine handcrafted financial features are encoded into a ZZFeatureMap quantum feature map; the paper does not specify a qubit-per-feature mapping beyond the feature map construction.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of whether a sector's 5-day cumulative return exceeds the equal-weighted market average 5-day cumulative return.

problem_instance.description: Sector rotation prediction across 10 Fama–French industries using daily returns from 2022-01-01 to 2024-12-31.

dataset_specification.preprocessing: chronological split; first 80% training, last 20% testing; Z-score standardization using training statistics only; quantum reference set restricted to first 100 chronologically sorted training samples

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Constructed nine features from the past 60 trading days: mean return, volatility, win rate, excess return, MA5, MA20, max drawdown, 5-day return, and skewness. Labels defined by whether sector 5-day cumulative return exceeds market average 5-day cumulative return.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Accuracy on the test set for each sector; average accuracy and standard deviation across all 10 sectors.

implementation_details.framework_version: Qiskit Machine Learning v0.8.4; scikit-learn v1.7.2; Python 3.12
implementation_details.classical_solver: scikit-learn SVC (RBF and linear kernels) as baselines; 1-NN for quantum kernel post-processing
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: StandardScaler fit on training data only; chronological split; deterministic selection of first 100 training samples for quantum reference set
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Kernel matrix computed via ComputeUncompute fidelity estimation; 1-NN assigns label of most similar training reference sample

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports empirical accuracy comparisons only and does not claim or demonstrate an asymptotic or runtime speedup.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not established; the quantum method used a simulator with a 100-sample reference set and 1-NN post-processing, while classical SVC baselines used the full training set.
limiting_factors: Classical RBF kernel achieved the best mean accuracy at 52.1% versus 50.0% for the quantum kernel.
Quantum kernel only outperformed classical methods in 2 of 10 sectors.
Quantum evaluation used only 100 reference samples, so the comparison is not fully matched to the classical baselines.
No asymptotic or runtime speedup is claimed or demonstrated.

notes: hardware.type inferred as simulator_statevector because the paper states AerSimulator with statevector simulation and no real QPU.
num_qubits not explicitly reported; likely equals the feature-map register size but the paper does not state the qubit count, so left null.
circuit_depth not explicitly given as a numeric depth; reps=1 is reported and used as a shallow circuit proxy, but actual depth is not stated.
No asymptotic quantum/classical speedup order is characterized in the paper; only empirical accuracy comparisons are provided.
The paper explicitly reports that classical RBF has the highest average accuracy (52.1%), while the quantum kernel reaches 50.0% and is only best in two sectors.
